apps.author: markqvist
apps.name: Sideband
apps.changeLog:
This release adds easier half-duplex voice link establishment, the ability to load custom interfaces on Android, and improves overall voice functionality and handling. It also includes the latest versions of RNS, LXMF and LXST with all the improvements from those releases.

To load custom interfaces on Android, make sure you have a plugins directory configured, and place any required interfaces in the `interfaces` subdirectory. Sideband will then load them on startup.

**Changes**
- Added ability to load custom interfaces from configured plugins directory on Android
- Added voice link establishment from conversations screen
- Added LXMF PTT high-quality/low-bandwidth quick switcher to messages screen
- Added propagation node version information to announce stream details
- Added version information to discovered interface details
- Improved call and voice link handling
- Significantly improved delivery reliability and efficiency over extreme link conditions
- Fixed outgoing audio not working on Android if call was accepted while or shortly after app was in background
- Updates repository assets and docs to latest versions
- Updated RNS to 1.5.5, LXMF to 1.2.0 and LXST to 0.5.4

## Eridanus 0.3.1

### Which APK?

Eridanus ships two flavors, one running the official Reticulum reference implementation, 
and another running an unfinished, experimental, mostly AI-generated port of Reticulum to kotlin. 
Both aspire to behave identically and both
attach to a shared Reticulum instance on your device ([Sideband](https://github.com/markqvist/Sideband),
rnsd in Termux, [Reticulum-for-Android](https://github.com/torlando-tech/reticulum-android)). The only
_intended_ difference is *which Reticulum implementation runs in-process*:

| APK | Reticulum implementation | Size |
|-----|--------------------------|------|
| **eridanus-python-0.3.1.apk** | upstream python Reticulum, embedded via chaquopy — the reference implementation | larger (bundles a Python runtime) |
| **eridanus-kotlin-0.3.1.apk** | reticulum-kt (experimental kotlin port, WIP, AI-Generated) | smaller |

The Python version is highly recommended, unless you are willing to experiment and are open to the risks of missing or broken behavior at the cryptography layers,
and really need the smaller APK.
### Installation
Download one APK and install on your Android device (Android 8.0+).

## Columba 2.2.6

### What's new in v2.2.x
This stable release includes the following new features since v2.0.9:

- voice call history screen
- voice message attachments, interopable with sideband and meshchatx
- displays LXMF resource transfer progress in message bubbles
- export columba's shared reticulum instance config
- in-app theme override (set dark mode even if your system is light or doesn't expose system level theme)
- RNode battery level displayed on interface card and persistent notification
- nomadnet truecolor support and newlines in form fields
- experimental pyxis flasher
- renders incoming markdown messages as markdown (no support for sending markdown LXMF messages yet)

Plus tons of bug fixes, especially around BLE RNode handling, reconnecting and recovering from disconnects. Also several performance and stability improvements.

I've removed the kotlin backend from this release, as it is not stable. 


### Installation
Download the APK matching your device's CPU architecture.

| APK | Architecture | Devices |
|-----|-------------|---------|
| [`columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-armeabi-v7a.apk`](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/download/v2.2.6/columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-armeabi-v7a.apk) | armeabi-v7a | Older 32-bit ARM phones & tablets |
| [`columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-arm64-v8a.apk`](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/download/v2.2.6/columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-arm64-v8a.apk) | arm64-v8a | Most modern Android phones & tablets |
| [`columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-x86_64.apk`](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/download/v2.2.6/columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-x86_64.apk) | x86_64 | Chromebooks, emulators, some tablets |
| [`columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-universal.apk`](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/download/v2.2.6/columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-universal.apk) | All | Universal fallback (larger download) |


**Telemetry variants:**
Each APK above also has a `-no-sentry` variant without crash reporting for maximum privacy — append `-no-sentry` to any download link above (e.g. the most common builds: [Python arm64-v8a no-sentry](https://github.com/torlando-tech/columba/releases/download/v2.2.6/columba-2.2.6-official-rns-py-arm64-v8a-no-sentry.apk)). Sentry collects stack traces when Columba encounters errors
and provides helpful information to the developer to improve Columba, but is hosted at sentry.io, and is thus not the maximum privacy option.

> **Not sure which to pick?** Most Android phones use **arm64-v8a**. If unsure, use the **universal** APK.

apps.author: Quad4-Software
apps.name: MeshChatX
apps.changeLog:
Release Notes ### Added - Traffic tools: sustained high traffic now raises a warning in the log and on the Traffic page, naming the component (LXMF, RRC, NomadNet, crawler) or the wire total when the load is announces, path requests, or forwarding. Warnings are rate limited so a flood cannot flood the log. - Traffic tools: active transfers now show with progress, covering RNCP file transfers and file sync. Their bytes are metered as they move, so the component table names them instead of hiding them in the residual row. - Traffic tools: hovering the chart shows the upload and download rates at that point in time and which component was driving them. Both series now share one vertical scale so their heights compare honestly. ### Fixed - Relay chat: delivered messages no longer show "not delivered to hub" after a restart or reconnect. Echo confirmations are now persisted, a late echo restores a failed row instead of counting it as a repeat, and the client asks the hub which sends it already relayed on rejoin (T_SYNC/T_SEEN) so delivered rows heal without resending. - Relay chat: messages sent to a room the client has not joined are now confirmed by a direct hub receipt instead of always expiring as failed. - Profile: clearing the display name no longer claims an auto-save and then brings the old name back. The field keeps what you are typing, an empty name sent by any client resets to the default name, and leaving the field empty restores the saved name with a notice. - Relay chat: the available rooms section remembers whether it was collapsed or expanded when you navigate away and come back. Mount time auto-selection no longer overwrites the saved layout before it is restored. - Relay chat: unreachable hubs no longer spray mesh wide path requests while the reconnect backoff grows. Each hub gets a small burst for the first attempt, then at most one request per minute. - Settings: the auto announce interval and the propagation auto sync interval now clamp to a one minute minimum instead of accepting sub-minute values that turn announces and mailbox syncs into mesh wide storms. - Relay chat: the log now names the hub when a send budget blocks, warns when a message keeps getting redelivered, and reports how many held messages a rejoin resent. - Messages: the log warns when a destination has exhausted its auto-resend budget and messages need a manual retry. - File sync: the announce interval setter now enforces the same one minute floor the loader and the UI already use, so an API request can no longer set a sub-minute announce storm. - Traffic tools: the hover guide and dots on the activity chart are round again on wide windows. They now render outside the stretched chart area instead of being squished by it. - Remote execute: listener sessions now surface their address even when quiet mode suppresses rnx log output. The manager derives the rnx.execute destination hash from the identity file instead of waiting for a log line that may never come. - Tools: rnsh and rnx are out of alpha. Both are covered by live network tests that run a real listener and initiator over a loopback Reticulum link, including the frozen app launcher path. - NomadNet browser: multi-line form fields on pages now accept and submit line breaks again. The bundled micron WASM renderer ignored the field row count and drew a single-line box, so posts submitted through forms arrived as one long line. Lines carrying multi-row fields now render through the JS parser on any WASM version, and the bundled renderer is updated to v1.3.0 which draws the textbox correctly on its own.

apps.changeLog:
## v1.0.35

### Added

- Added Auto-Lock for passcode-protected identities.
- Added a setting for how much notifications show.

### Fixed and improved

- Improved Bluetooth on Android: radios reconnect faster and show why they can't connect.
- Fixed pairing a radio again after removing it from Android's Bluetooth settings.
- Radios that reject a setting now say which one.
- Improved identity switching, so messages and contacts always stay with the right identity.
- Showing your recovery phrase or exporting a key now asks for your PIN, and copied phrases clear after a minute.
- Fixed a file name bug when exporting on desktop.
- Fixed recovery phrases not being saved in rare cases.
- Improved compatibility with the latest Python Reticulum and LXMF.
- Fixed downloading messages from propagation nodes that hold many messages.
- Fixed game boards being cut off on phones; games now open full screen.
- Made captured chess pieces and game results easier to see.

### Build and compatibility

- Linux: USB radios are now available only to the signed-in user. The rule is now `70-ratspeak.rules`; delete any old `99-ratspeak.rules` you copied by hand.
